title: Towards an Automated Workflow for Floating-Point Analysis of GPU Kernels
problem: GPU kernel floating-point error analysis is critical for scientific accuracy but lacks automated, standardized workflows. Existing approaches require manual kernel modification or don't support diverse precision modes (FP16, TF32, BF16), limiting applicability.
motivation: Scientific GPU applications require rigorous floating-point accuracy evaluation, but current methods are labor-intensive and inflexible. Need for automated tools to evaluate accuracy across precision modes and optimizations.
method: Automated workflow leveraging Intercept Layer for OpenCL Applications to record GPU kernel execution and replay on CPU runtimes. Uses PoCL and Verificarlo for detailed floating-point error analysis. Supports IEEE-compliant and reduced-precision modes (FP16, TF32, BF16). Evaluates -ffast-math effects using stochastic arithmetic (MCA) and PRISM.
key_novelty: First automated workflow enabling GPU kernel floating-point analysis without source modification; supports reduced-precision modes and compiler optimizations; leverages open tools and standards.
contributions: Automated floating-point error analysis workflow for SYCL kernels
GPU-to-CPU replay mechanism via Intercept Layer
Support for diverse precision modes (IEEE, FP16, TF32, BF16)
limitations: Single case study (HACC force kernel) limits generalizability
Performance overhead of CPU replay not discussed
Scalability to large-scale production kernels not demonstrated
